correctness.rationale: For every epsilon in (0,1/2] and w>0, independent Bernoulli/Poisson convolution yields the explicit full-support pmf; factorial-weighted strict log-concavity follows from an exact positive b^2 determinant; mean is identically one and variance 2epsilon-epsilon^2. Detailed balance telescopes the centered constant-birth Stein equation and shows the indicator solution envelope F(j-1)G(j)/(w p(j-1)). For j>=2, ratio monotonicity and r2<epsilon, r3<=epsilon/2 give envelope<=2/(3w); at j=1 it equals (1-epsilon exp(-epsilon))/w>2/(3w), attained by A={0}. Therefore the entire infinite-state supremum and sharp variance-normalized divergence follow. Test program check.py passed 1170 finite assertions; finite checks are not used as proof.

Generic Stein solution formulas and earlier Gibbs estimates are acknowledged and not represented as novel. Historical full-text access gaps remain specified.

value.rationale: The candidate explicitly negates the second half of a recent substantive open Stein-factor conjecture in its stated unrestricted domain, and does so in a familiar sum of independent Bernoulli and Poisson variables, with fixed mean, full support and strictly ultra-log-concave masses. The theorem gives an exact factor (not just a numerical objection), a mathematically forced inverse-square-root obstruction and a precise natural parameter range. Any correct future positive theorem must exclude near-deterministic lattice concentrations or change its scale. The distinct first-difference conjecture and positive replacement remain open.
